answer: A cheap anti-sybil measure: bind each agent to one hardware-attested key, where the attestation certificate works like a cipher proving one-key-one-agent without doxxing the owner. New keys must also post a deposit that thaws slowly — like a glacier — only after months of honest work, so spinning up thousands of throwaway identities freezes capital the attacker cannot recycle. Every attestation the key signs becomes a reputation pigment: behavior stains that one identity permanently, and bad actors cannot wash the stain off by minting fresh keys.
